survey: A shallow, clear glass plate sits flat on a wooden table, seen from slightly above and in front. Its rim is a wide, even ellipse. On the plate, back to front: 1) A watermelon wedge stands upright at the back. Its red flesh faces the camera, the green rind is on the right, and its base rests on the plate behind the other fruit. Its seeds point the same way, as real seeds do. 2) A bunch of green grapes sits on the left of the plate. A woody stem with a leaf rises from the top of the bunch and tucks behind the watermelon's edge, so it attaches to the bunch and does not end in the air. 3) Two strawberries sit in the middle, each with a green cap. One is in front of the grapes and one is behind it. 4) Four blueberries lie in a cluster on the plate floor at the front, each with a crown-shaped end. 5) Two orange wedges lean against the watermelon on the right. Their peel faces down and right, with flesh segments showing. Every piece rests either on the plate or on a neighbouring fruit. The front strawberry's tip shows through the transparent front rim, which glass would allow, so it is not floating or passing through anything. No extra or invented parts, and the counts are plausible.
